title: Waves Call Extraction — Model Output
description: Schema for the JSON output Gemini produces from a call transcript. Excludes server-owned metadata fields (call_id, schema_version, extracted_at, extraction_model) which are injected after model response.

is_voicemail.description: True if the recording is a voicemail message rather than a two-party conversation.

is_spam.description: True if the call is spam, solicitation, robocall, or wrong number.

call_summary.description: 2-3 sentence summary of the call for quick triage.

name_full.description: Full name as spoken. Do not split or reformat.

first_name.description: First/given name if clearly identifiable. null if ambiguous or not stated.

last_name.description: Last/family name if clearly identifiable. Do not invent from caller ID, address, or context.

organization_name.description: Business or HOA name if caller is representing an organization.

name_confidence.description: Confidence that name extraction is correct. Low when spelled out ambiguously or only partially heard.

phone_e164.description: Best callback number stated by caller. May differ from Twilio ANI.

phone_raw_spoken.description: Phone number as spoken in transcript, verbatim. e.g. 'five five five, one two three, four five six seven'.

phone_source.description: How the phone number was obtained. 'caller_id' = from Twilio ANI only, 'spoken' = caller stated it, 'both' = matches ANI and spoken.

caller_id_disclaimed.description: 1.14.0 additive. true ONLY when the caller explicitly states the number reaching us is NOT their own — a shared/office line, a receptionist's desk phone, someone else's cell they borrowed. null when the call gives no signal either way; false is never set (the model omits the field or returns null instead — an unstated caller ID is not evidence it IS theirs). The Twilio ANI must not be trusted as a personal callback number when true and no spoken number backs it up; see phone_source and phone_note.

phone_note.description: 1.14.0 additive. The caller's own words explaining the number, verbatim or lightly trimmed (e.g. "this is our office line, they route calls to me and I text back"). Only set alongside caller_id_disclaimed=true. null when nothing was said about the number itself.

email.description: Email address as heard, even if the domain sounds incomplete (e.g. 'brandon@gmail'). Server re-validates and repairs known domain typos; an invalid capture must not be dropped here.

on_site_authorization.description: Caller has affirmed authority to authorize service at the property. MUST be true to clear auto-appointment gate when caller != owner.

decision_maker_present.description: Caller can commit to service/pricing without consulting another party.

secondary_contact.description: A SECOND person named as a party to the service (a realtor's home buyer, a landlord's tenant, a spouse). null when no such person was named. The caller's own identity always stays in `caller`. 1.2.0 additive — absent in older payloads. phone_e164/email are deliberately unpatterned here: a garbled spoken value must not schema-fail the whole extraction; the server normalizer validates and nulls them.

phone_e164.description: Callback number stated for this person, E.164 preferred. Server re-validates.

email.description: Only when clearly said or spelled in full. Server re-validates.

role.description: This person's relationship to the transaction — the BUYER a realtor books for is home_buyer, not real_estate_agent.

wants_notifications.description: true ONLY when the caller explicitly directed notifications/confirmations/updates to this person. A merely-mentioned or explicitly-excluded person is false.

wants_appointment_texts.description: 1.22.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true ONLY when the caller agreed THIS person should receive the appointment TEXT messages (visit reminders, the 'on the way'/route-tracking link, the arrival text). Wanting the report or invoice emailed to them is NOT enough — false. Default false; do not invent. Needs an evidence quote when true.

on_site.description: 1.22.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true ONLY when the call says THIS person will be AT the property for the visit (lives there, 'he'll be there', meeting the technician). A relationship alone does not prove presence — false. Default false; do not invent. Needs an evidence quote when true.

is_billing_party.description: true ONLY when the caller clearly says THIS person pays for the service (e.g. 'the owner Jim will pay by credit card', 'bill the management company'). Merely being the owner/landlord/manager is NOT enough — the caller must indicate they cover the cost. 1.6.0 additive; absent in older payloads.

secondary_contacts.description: ALL other people named as parties to the service, most notification-central first (up to 3). The FIRST entry must also mirror into secondary_contact for older readers. []/null when no other party was named. 1.4.0 additive - absent in older payloads.

phone_e164.description: Callback number stated for this person, E.164 preferred. Server re-validates.

email.description: Only when clearly said or spelled in full. Server re-validates.

wants_notifications.description: true ONLY when the caller explicitly directed notifications/confirmations/updates to THIS person.

wants_appointment_texts.description: 1.22.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true ONLY when the caller agreed THIS person should receive the appointment TEXT messages (visit reminders, the 'on the way'/route-tracking link, the arrival text). Wanting the report or invoice emailed to them is NOT enough — false. Default false; do not invent. Needs an evidence quote when true.

on_site.description: 1.22.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true ONLY when the call says THIS person will be AT the property for the visit (lives there, 'he'll be there', meeting the technician). A relationship alone does not prove presence — false. Default false; do not invent. Needs an evidence quote when true.

is_billing_party.description: true ONLY when the caller clearly says THIS person pays for the service (e.g. 'the owner Jim pays by credit card', 'bill the management company'). Merely being the owner/landlord/manager is NOT enough. 1.6.0 additive.

consent.description: TCPA-relevant consent capture. SMS dispatch MUST check sms_consent_given=true and do_not_contact_request=false before firing.

sms_consent_quote.description: Verbatim transcript span where consent was given.

do_not_contact_request.description: Caller explicitly asked not to be contacted further.

sms_declined.description: Additive (schema 1.19.0) — optional, not required: true ONLY if the caller explicitly declines text messages (says no when asked to be texted, or asks not to be texted / to be called instead of texted), even if calls are fine. false otherwise, including when texting never came up. ALWAYS output true or false — never null, even though the type allows it: null exists only so historical payloads validate (a pre-1.19 extraction never has this field at all). Distinct from sms_consent_given=false, which merely means consent was never asked.

raw_text.description: Address as spoken by the caller, verbatim. Preserved for re-extraction and audit.

county.description: County of the service address. Manatee, Sarasota and Charlotte are served; DeSoto may be emitted as a county value but is NOT in the service area (owner ruling 2026-09-30), so a DeSoto address must set triage_flag=out_of_service_area. Any other county also sets out_of_service_area unless it is a served south-Hillsborough town.

normalization_status.description: Set by server after normalization pass. Model should output 'not_attempted'.

hoa_community_flag.description: Property sits within an HOA community. Not the same as HOA common-area service.

hoa_common_area_service.description: Service is for HOA-owned common areas. Triggers commercial pricing + admin-approval hold.

bedroom_count.description: Bedroom count of the caller's dwelling UNIT (apartment/condo) as SPOKEN on the call — 'one-bedroom' = 1, 'studio' = 0. null unless stated. Never infer from square footage, rent, or property type.

species_notes.description: Free text: 'two dogs in yard', 'indoor cat', 'koi pond'.

access_notes.description: Gate code, side gate locked, dogs in back, lockbox info.

additional_properties.description: OTHER properties the caller wants serviced or discussed owning (second home, rental, another unit). The primary property stays in service_address; every additional one goes here. Empty when only one property is discussed.

notes.description: What the caller said about this property: services wanted, access, exterior covered by HOA, etc.

is_primary_residence.description: true ONLY when the caller states/strongly implies THIS property is their main home; false when stated otherwise; null when unstated.

service_address_occupancy.description: Occupancy of the MAIN service_address when the caller states or strongly implies it; null when unstated.

service_address_is_primary_residence.description: true ONLY when the caller states/strongly implies the service_address is the home they LIVE in as their main residence; false when they state it is not (rental, seasonal, tenant-occupied); null when unstated.

pests_observed_status.description: Semantic status. 'observed' = pests_observed has items. 'not_observed_preventative' = wants prevention, no active pest. 'not_observed_inquiry' = quote/info call. 'not_discussed' = call topic didn't involve pest identification.

specific_service_name.description: Verbatim name from the bookable service catalog list in the prompt when the request maps to one specific bookable service; null otherwise. Never a name outside that list.

quoted_price_usd.description: Total USD price the agent quoted AND the caller accepted for the service being booked. null when no price was quoted/accepted or the amount is uncertain.

price_offered_by_staff.description: 1.21.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true ONLY when a Waves staff member (speaker "agent") OFFERED the amount in service_request.quoted_price_usd as Waves' OWN quote for this service: a statement of the price ("that runs $150", "it's $150 a visit"), never a question about a price ("did another company quote you $150?"), never a competitor's or the caller's number, never a hypothetical or a range. Pin the staff's price sentence to /service_request/price_offered_by_staff with speaker "agent"; the amount must appear in that quote exactly as spoken, digits or words ("$149" or "one hundred forty-nine dollars"); never rewrite words as digits. false when the amount was not offered that way; null when no price was discussed.

price_accepted_by_caller.description: 1.21.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true ONLY when the CALLER, in their own words, accepted THAT staff-offered price: agreement with the amount itself ("yes, that works", "okay, $150 is fine", "let's do it"). false when the caller objected, negotiated, asked a question instead, agreed to something else (a time, a different service), or accepted only part of it ("that works for the price, but ..." the price part counts only if the rest does not take it back). The acceptance must come AFTER the staff's offer. Pin the caller's acceptance to /service_request/price_accepted_by_caller with speaker "caller". null when no price was discussed.

price_is_final.description: 1.21.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true ONLY when the accepted amount was the LAST price staff stated for this service on the call: with nothing added to it: no later correction, revision, different number or ADDED CHARGE, in any amount and any phrasing, before the call ended ("actually, correction, it's $250", "plus ten dollars for the garage", "that is before the trip fee"). false when staff or the caller changed the price or a charge was added between the offer and the acceptance OR after it, even a small one. When in doubt, false. null when no price was discussed.

quote_requested.description: Getting a quote/estimate/pricing was a reason for the call.

quote_promised.description: The AGENT committed to send a quote/estimate after the call. Means work is still owed to the caller — set even when an appointment was also booked.

price.description: The PRIMARY price stated on the call by either party (the accepted one if any, else the first stated) — distinct from quoted_price_usd, which stays the narrower accepted-total-only field. When more than one distinct price was stated (e.g. a one-time price AND a monthly price), every one of them also goes in the sibling `prices` array with the primary entry FIRST (prices[0]), and this field is always a copy of that entry — the two fields agree by construction, never by a separate ordering rule. Optional: omit or leave every field null when no price was discussed.

amount_usd.description: The stated price, or the LOW end when a range was given. null when no number was stated. Never estimate or invent a price.

amount_max_usd.description: The HIGH end of a stated range (e.g. '$90 to 100 per quarter' -> amount_usd 90, amount_max_usd 100). null when a single number was given, not a range.

unit.description: The billing unit AS SPOKEN (e.g. 'per application', 'a quarter', 'a year'). 'unknown' when a price was stated but no unit was said; null when no price was stated.

accepted.description: DERIVED from caller_response — kept only for backward compatibility with readers written before caller_response existed; set both consistently. true when caller_response is 'accepted'. false when caller_response is 'declined' or 'no_response'. null when caller_response is 'not_at_issue' or null/absent. This schema does not itself enforce the derivation — normalizeExtractionV2 (server/utils/normalize-extraction-v2.js) recomputes `accepted` from `caller_response` before persistence whenever caller_response is present, so a model that returns a disagreeing pair is corrected rather than trusted as-is.

caller_response.description: The CALLER's explicit response to this price — replaces the old boolean-only accepted signal, which conflated "declined" with "never responded". 'accepted' when the caller agreed to it. 'declined' when the caller said no / pushed back and it was not resolved to yes. 'no_response' when the agent stated it and the call moved on (hung up, changed subject) before the caller reacted either way. 'not_at_issue' when acceptance was never in play (e.g. caller only asked "what's the price for X" as a general question, or it's a competitor's price the caller is just quoting back). null when the call did not address the question at all.

stated_by.description: Who said the number first — almost always 'agent'; 'caller' when the caller quoted a price back (e.g. a competitor's price, or repeating what they read online).

prepay_term.description: 'annual' when paying for the year up front was discussed ('pay the year', 'annual prepay'); 'none' when prepay was explicitly ruled out; null when never discussed.

tier_mentioned.description: A WaveGuard package tier name mentioned in connection with THIS price, by either party. Independent of waveguard_tier_mentioned (which is caller-sourced only).

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim transcript quote the price fields above were read from. null when price is otherwise empty.

prices.description: EVERY DISTINCT price stated on the call (one-time, monthly, a competitor's price, etc.), ordered with the PRIMARY entry FIRST — the accepted one if any, else the first price stated on the call — followed by the remaining distinct prices in the order stated. `price` (the sibling field above) is always a copy of prices[0] under this ordering — a single ordering rule, not two that can disagree. A call with only one price mentioned may leave this empty or omit it; `price` alone still carries it. Each entry has the same shape as `price`. This schema does not itself enforce that `price` matches prices[0] — normalizeExtractionV2 (server/utils/normalize-extraction-v2.js) canonicalizes `price` from a nonempty `prices` before persistence (merging rather than replacing when they describe the same price), so a model that returns a disagreeing pair is corrected rather than trusted as-is.

amount_usd.description: The stated price, or the LOW end when a range was given. null when no number was stated. Never estimate or invent a price.

amount_max_usd.description: The HIGH end of a stated range. null when a single number was given, not a range.

unit.description: The billing unit AS SPOKEN. 'unknown' when a price was stated but no unit was said; null when no price was stated.

accepted.description: DERIVED from caller_response — see the same field on `price`.

caller_response.description: The CALLER's explicit response to THIS price — see the same field on `price`.

stated_by.description: Who said the number first — almost always 'agent'; 'caller' when the caller quoted a price back.

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim transcript quote this entry's price fields were read from.

status.description: Only 'confirmed' maps to legacy appointment_confirmed=true. 'requested'/'offered' do NOT create appointments.

confirmed_start_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime with the Eastern Time offset (never UTC 'Z'). Set when status='confirmed' AND both specific date AND specific time agreed, or when a reschedule concluded with a new agreed date+time (status='reschedule_requested' — carries the NEW slot for the office to move the existing visit to).

proposed_start_at.description: The caller's one specifically requested NEW reschedule date and time, ISO 8601 with Eastern offset. Not an agreement. Null for vague or competing alternatives. Pin the caller's date/time quote to /scheduling/proposed_start_at.

agent_committed_booking.description: true ONLY when OUR agent, in the agent's own words, explicitly committed to the confirmed slot ("we'll confirm it for noon on Sunday", "you're on the schedule"). The caller requesting, agreeing, or asserting a commitment is never an agent commitment. null when unclear.

caller_accepted_slot.description: Booking or reschedule that ENDS with an agreed slot: true ONLY when the CALLER, in the caller's own words, accepted that FINAL slot (or asked for exactly that slot and the agent committed to it), judged over the whole call; false when the caller later withdrew, changed, conditioned, or questioned it, or left the agent's proposal unanswered. The agent's words never count. Pin the caller's acceptance to /scheduling/caller_accepted_slot. null when no slot was agreed or it is unclear.

moved_appointment_date.description: Reschedule only: the calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD, Eastern) of the EXISTING appointment being moved, as established on the call by either speaker. Pin the utterance naming it to /scheduling/moved_appointment_date. null when the call never identifies which existing appointment is being moved — never inferred from the new slot.

agreed_slot_words.description: Set ONLY when confirmed_start_at is set: the agreed START time's words, copied VERBATIM (exact characters as they appear in the transcript) from the /scheduling/confirmed_start_at evidence quote, which must contain every non-null value here. hour: the word(s) naming the agreed START hour exactly as spoken ("two", "2", "10", "noon", "midnight") — only the hour, no minutes, no AM/PM; for an arrival window, the window's start ("between two and four" -> "two"). period: the words stating AM/PM for THAT hour ("pm", "p.m.", "in the afternoon", "this evening", "tonight") — null when nobody said AM/PM or a part of day for that time (never write a period nobody said: an hour said without AM/PM is read as business hours by the prompt rule — 7-11 morning, 12 and 1-6 afternoon — for a new booking or a reschedule, with period null; and never a part of day describing the OLD appointment, e.g. "your morning appointment"); null for noon/midnight. day: the words naming the agreed day ("Thursday", "tomorrow", "tonight", "November 9th", "the 9th") — null when the day was not said because only the time of the same-day appointment changes (or, for a new booking, because the turn holding the agreed hour does not repeat the day). Set the whole object null (and do not confirm) when the agreed time is not ONE exact on-the-hour start: approximate ("two-ish", "around noonish"), a bound ("before noon", "by two", "two or later"), alternatives ("two or four"), or has minutes ("two thirty"). When a speaker corrected the time, use the FINAL corrected words only ("at two, actually three" -> hour "three").

moved_appointment_words.description: For status "reschedule_requested" ONLY: the verbatim words from the /scheduling/moved_appointment_date evidence quote that name that date ("the 24th", "September 24th", "Thursday") — that quote must contain them exactly. null whenever moved_appointment_date is null.

definite_commitment.description: 1.20.0, additive/optional (never `required`): the extraction's judgement of the agent's promise for the agreed slot. true when the agent's own words firmly commit to that day and time. false ONLY when a hedge or condition applies to WHETHER or WHEN the appointment happens: could/might/can-try/probably/possibly/tentatively/hopefully/perhaps, a condition on the slot ("if ...", "once ...", "upon ...", "pending ...", "after the rain", "weather permitting"), or a plan still to be checked. A courtesy or contingency line about a LATER follow-up ("if anything comes up I'll let you know", "we'll text you a confirmation", "that should be fine" said after a firm slot) does not make it false. Prefer false when genuinely unsure. The agent's commitment quote (/scheduling/agent_committed_booking) must be the WHOLE clause holding the day, date and time INCLUDING every qualifier around them. null when no slot was agreed.

relative_date_used.description: 1.20.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true when the agreed slot's day was expressed relative to the call or to another date rather than as a plain weekday, calendar date, today, tomorrow or "this <weekday>": next week, the following Thursday, the Thursday after this one, a week from Thursday, eight days from now / away / out, in two weeks. Resolve it against the call date so confirmed_start_at carries the true absolute date, record only the bare weekday in agreed_slot_words.day when a weekday was said (otherwise the exact relative phrase, verbatim; the verifier computes only tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, in N days/weeks and N days/weeks from now/today, N = digits, "a"/"one", or two to eight, and sends any other weekday-less relative date to the office), and pin the whole clause holding the relative expression to /scheduling/relative_date_used. Prefer true when unsure. false when the day was a plain weekday/date/today/tomorrow. null when no slot was agreed.

moved_appointment_relative_date_used.description: 1.20.0, additive/optional (never `required`): true when the EXISTING appointment's day (moved_appointment_date) was expressed relative to the call or to another date rather than as a plain weekday, calendar date, today, tomorrow or "this <weekday>": next week, the following Thursday, the Thursday after this one, a week from Thursday, eight days from now / away / out, in two weeks. Resolve it against the call date so moved_appointment_date carries the true absolute date, record only the bare weekday in moved_appointment_words when a weekday was said (otherwise the exact relative phrase, same closed forms), and pin the whole clause holding the relative expression to /scheduling/moved_appointment_relative_date_used. Prefer true when unsure. false when the day was a plain weekday/date/today/tomorrow. null when no slot was agreed.

staff_accepted_proposed_slot.description: 1.21.0, additive/optional (never `required`): for a booking whose slot was PROPOSED by the caller (one exact day and on-the-hour time in the caller's turn, e.g. "Can you come Thursday at 2?"), true ONLY when the very next turn is staff's reply that accepts that whole proposal as stated ("Sure, that works."): not partially ("that works for the price, but the time is bad"), not with a change, condition or question, not a refusal. Pin the ENTIRE staff reply turn, verbatim, to /scheduling/staff_accepted_proposed_slot with speaker "agent" (also pin it as /scheduling/agent_committed_booking), and pin the caller's proposal turn as /scheduling/confirmed_start_at and /scheduling/caller_accepted_slot with speaker "caller". false when the reply did anything else; null when the caller did not propose the slot.

selected_day_words.description: 1.21.0, additive/optional (never `required`): for a NEW booking whose final time turn does not repeat the day (agreed_slot_words.day is null), the verbatim words naming the day the CALLER SELECTED as the final agreed day ("Thursday", "October 24th", "tomorrow"), copied exactly from a CALLER turn and pinned to /scheduling/selected_day_words with speaker "caller". Only a day the caller chose or agreed to: never a day the caller rejected, called impossible, or offered as one option among several, and never a relative day ("next Thursday"). null when agreed_slot_words.day is set or no day was selected.

follow_up_mentioned.description: true ONLY when a second/follow-up treatment visit was specifically discussed as part of this booking (e.g. a two-treatment protocol). A generic 'call us if it comes back' is not a follow-up visit.

follow_up_start_at.description: ISO 8601 Eastern Time datetime ONLY when a specific follow-up date/time was explicitly agreed; null otherwise.

evidence.description: Verbatim transcript spans for routing-critical fields. Pin evidence for: address, urgency, on_site_authorization, hoa_common_area_service, sms_consent_given, scheduling.status=confirmed, scheduling.agent_committed_booking=true (AGENT-spoken quote), scheduling.caller_accepted_slot=true (CALLER-spoken quote), scheduling.moved_appointment_date (the utterance naming it), scheduling.relative_date_used=true and scheduling.moved_appointment_relative_date_used=true (the whole clause holding the relative expression).

triage_flags.description: Model-suggested reasons the call should not auto-route. Server also computes deterministic flags after extraction — final gate uses the union.

other_parties_mentioned.description: true when the call names MORE people as parties to the service than the single secondary_contact captured (buyer + co-buyer + agent; tenant + owner) — tells the office to re-listen for the additional parties. null/false otherwise. 1.2.0 additive.

call_nature.description: Primary nature of the call — drives the terminal disposition. Null only when truly indeterminate.

recommended_disposition.description: Model-recommended terminal disposition. The rules layer may override; ambiguity resolves to lead_response_flow_triggered, never a review queue.

is_spam_content.description: Transcript CONTENT is solicitation/robocall/scam TO the business. Never true when a service request, service address, or quoted price is present.

evidence.description: <=20 words from the transcript supporting the verdict.

language.description: Caller language; spanish/other flags the language-support lane.
